errors.english: Even if there is a gathering, because there is no transformation, there is no contradiction in the eternity of the essence of cognition.
errors.why: 'du ba here is samavāya (inherence) in the Nyāya self-theory, and the clause says the transformation of cognition's nature does not contradict the self's permanence; this whole passage is the opponent's view, voiced before སྙམ་དུ་སེམས་པ་ལ, but the English gives it as an assertion.

errors.english: One who remains connected to both former and latter times is not perceived through direct perception because they do not occur in sequence.
errors.why: The Tibetan has a word gloss ('the abider connected with former and later times') and then a separate opponent's claim ('it is not perception, because it is not sequential'). The English merges them into one statement and drops the fact that someone else is speaking.

note: It follows the commentary's glosses reasonably, but the Nyāya self-theory section blurs the terms and who is speaking.

errors.english: You have heard words from the Noble Udāyin that we never even heard from drunkards, gamblers, or bastards.
errors.why: The women say that WE have heard these words from Udāyin, not 'you'.

fix.find: You have heard words from the Noble Udāyin that we never even heard from drunkards, gamblers, or bastards.
fix.replace: We have heard from the Noble Udāyin words that we had never heard even from drunkards, gamblers, or bastards.

errors.english: corrupt words of a sinful nature
errors.why: The qualifier 'not to be uttered in company' (vulgar, indecent) is dropped, both in the narrative and in the rule's formula.

note: A sound rendering of the saṅghāvaśeṣa origin story and rule, apart from the women's speech switching to the wrong person.

errors.english: Furthermore, heaviness is not the result of sin, because perception and (non-perception) the logical proof of absence; original: mi dmigs pa are absent.
errors.why: The Tibetan marks this as a doubt someone raises (ཞེས་དོགས་པའོ), but the English presents it as the commentator's own assertion.

note: The argument against initiation removing sin is followed correctly; the inline glosses are cluttered but not wrong.

errors.english: entered exactly as the divine command had instructed
errors.why: In drama, ལྷ renders deva, 'Your Majesty'; Subāhu acts on the king's order, not on a divine command.

errors.english: come Hari [note: Vishnu]
errors.why: This is the Vedic subrahmaṇyā invocation of Indra (hari-vas, 'lord of the bay horses', with Medhātithi's ram), so the gloss Vishnu misleads.

note: A lively and faithful rendering of the drama scene; the problems are minor and confined to the ritual context.

errors.english: "By way of distinct clarity" means they are mutually exclusive.
errors.why: In this discussion of universals, གསལ་བ is vyakti, 'particular instance', not 'clarity'.

errors.english: If it is not so, and you think that because they are perceived
errors.why: The point is that the insects are cognized OTHERWISE (by a later contradicting cognition), so 'otherwise' is lost and the reasoning becomes incoherent.

errors.english: [note: original: ཁྲ་བོ་, refers to a composite color like brindled or multicolored]
errors.why: ཁྲ་བོ and སེར་སྐྱ are the standard brindled and tawny COWS (śābaleya/kapila) of the cowness-universal debate, not colours.

note: The outline of the argument survives, but the vocabulary of the universals debate (vyakti, the cow examples) is handled loosely.
A faithful and well-segmented rendering of Avalokitavrata's gloss on 'when debated by means of emptiness', with MMK 1.1 correctly kept as verse.

errors.english: Ka. [note: This letter marks the beginning of the section or volume.]
errors.why: ཀ་ནི is the tail of the interleaved Sanskrit verse line (…karṇikāni) and the side continues the lotus description ('golden … with filaments and anthers', གེ་སར་ཟེ་འབྲུ་ཅན), which is left untranslated; it does not mark a section.

fix.find: Ka. [note: This letter marks the beginning of the section or volume.] Then,

errors.english: the (Sugata) Well-Gone One; the Buddha was seen nearby, seated upon them
errors.why: Sugatacakra is a circle of Sugatas seated on the lotuses, and the Bhagavat is then 'in their midst'; the English makes it a single Buddha, so 'in the midst of them' loses its referent.

errors.english: like the (Parijata) the wish-fulfilling tree of the gods among the (Sura) demigods or celestial beings
errors.why: The simile, as the parallel Sanskrit surakṣitiruhām shows, is the pārijāta towering among the TREES of the gods, not among divine beings.

note: The Tibetan verse parts are followed in outline, but the bilingual layout is misread at the opening and several images are distorted.

errors.english: a mere demonstration of an "infinite jewel" that cures fever
errors.why: མཐའ་ཡས is the serpent-king Ananta: this is the stock example of the fever-curing jewel of a nāga king, a purpose that cannot be had, so it is a proper name, not 'infinite', and the accompanying note is off.

fix.find: a mere demonstration of an "infinite jewel" that cures fever
fix.replace: a mere description of the fever-curing jewel of the serpent-king Ananta

errors.english: just as engagement is brought about by removing misconceptions that lack purpose
errors.why: The PURPOSE prompts engagement by removing the false notion that there is NO purpose; the English loses the agent and turns the notion into 'misconceptions that lack purpose'.

fix.find: just as engagement is brought about by removing misconceptions that lack purpose
fix.replace: just as the purpose brings about engagement by removing the false notion that there is no purpose

errors.english: from the general authority of the treatise
errors.why: The phrase means 'with reference to treatises in general', in contrast to a purpose made specific through the subject matter; it is not about 'authority'.

errors.english: engagement occurs through a mistaken understanding of the lack of purpose; or, if not mistaken, it results in turning away
errors.why: ལོག་པ here is 'removed': when purposelessness is understood to be excluded one engages, and when it is not excluded one turns away. 'Mistaken understanding' inverts the logic.

note: A hard passage on prayojana and abhidheya: the gist is partly there, but the key examples and several argumentative steps are misread.

errors.english: With mouths filled with saliva, they drink from it as if from a vessel filled with wine.
errors.why: The deluded drink from (kiss) the beloved's mouth, full of saliva, as if it were a cup of wine; the saliva-filled mouth is the object, not the drinkers'.

fix.find: With mouths filled with saliva, they drink from it as if from a vessel filled with wine.
fix.replace: They drink from a mouth filled with saliva as if it were a vessel filled with wine.

errors.english: You have determined "I" and "mine"
errors.why: The subject who imagines subject and object and fixes 'I' and 'mine' is 'this deluded world', not 'you'.

note: A good verse rendering of the meditation on the body's impurity, with one misread image and one shifted subject.

span_why: The opening sentences ('To establish that this is the wrong time, three verses are spoken … not yet been reached') translate the previous side's last line.

errors.english: What was intended to be done at the very beginning is this composition.
errors.why: This glosses the root word 'this begun' (BCA 7.8) as whatever aim one first meant to undertake; བརྩམས་པ is 'begun', not 'this composition'.

fix.find: What was intended to be done at the very beginning is this composition.
fix.replace: "This begun" refers to whatever aim one intended to undertake first.

errors.english: Remaining dedicated to this purpose
errors.why: The root reads 'this only half done' (ཆེད for ཕྱེད), as the gloss 'something accomplished, something not' shows.

note: A faithful gloss-by-gloss rendering of the BCA commentary on sudden death, apart from the misread root words and the carried-over opening.
